=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Note on the Seller's covering material:** The Seller says its positions are "FINAL", were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "standard market terms". These are the other side's assertions, not established facts. Before treating any point as closed, please confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether anything was actually agreed. Absent written confirmation, I have treated every point as open.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts its SPA Update on several points:
- **Bluefen:** the Update says "addressed", but the letter says no consent has been obtained.
- **Riverlark:** the Update says "addressed", but the letter says the facility is not repaid and no discharge exists.
- **Bonuses:** the letter confirms the AUD 420,000 is not in the funds flow.
- **Incident:** the Update calls it "not expected to be material", but the letter says scope and access are unknown.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Clause 12.1 caps general Warranty Claims at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, around 30–50%, or 20% only if fundamental, tax and specific indemnities sit entirely outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 35%. Fall back to 20% only if SPA-N-004, 005, 011, 012 and 014 are won.
- **Reason:** A 20% cap is tolerable only if the known risks are ring-fenced. At present they are not, and Bluefen alone is about 30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000. Basket of AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of about AUD 10,000. Basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000) as a tipping basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the threshold is crossed. Related claims should be aggregated for the de minimis. None of this should apply to specific indemnities, tax, title or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible basket and counter with a tipping basket at 0.5% plus an aggregation language.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket of AUD 250k permanently forfeits real losses. Without aggregation, related items such as the 3 × AUD 110k Sandbar renewals could each be argued around.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so two full audit cycles post-Completion are covered. Tax claims should run about 5–7 years, or the statutory amendment period plus 6 months. Title should run about 7 years or the statutory limitation period. Specific indemnities should run until the underlying matter finally resolves.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months. Reverse the default so that general limits apply only to general Warranty Claims.
- **Reason:** 18 months covers only one audit. The "applies to all Claims" default silently shortens tax and indemnity protection.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances over the shares) capped at 100% of price (AUD 24m). No de minimis or basket. Long time limit. Not qualified by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, so a AUD 4.8m recovery is not a risk allocation.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct and wilful or deliberate concealment by the Seller, the Company or their representatives. It should also preserve statutory rights that cannot lawfully be excluded, including Australian Consumer Law s 18.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert a full fraud and wilful-concealment carve-out.
- **Reason:** The Buyer should not accept any limitation that purports to cap recovery for the Seller's fraud. This is non-negotiable.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. The letter also says it admits nothing, including materiality.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only matters fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact.
  - Specific disclosures only, made against specific warranties.
  - No general disclosure of the data room or public records.
  - Disclosure must not qualify fundamental warranties, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Strike paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2. Accept specific disclosures 2–10 only to the extent they are fair, and only against the relevant warranty.
- **Reason:** General data-room disclosure transfers every unidentified risk to the Buyer and hollows out the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 says the Buyer has no claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Express pro-sandbagging wording, so Buyer knowledge or investigation does not prejudice any claim. At most, as a fallback, exclude matters of which named Buyer deal-team individuals had actual knowledge. Never constructive or adviser knowledge, and never for specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter with a pro-sandbagging clause.
- **Reason:** As drafted, it would knock out the very risks the Buyer is protecting through specific indemnities, because the Buyer "knows" about them from due diligence.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Clauses 3 and 6.3 require only reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The letter confirms no consent exists and the clause 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent: unconditional written Bluefen consent under clause 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
  - The condition waivable only by the Buyer.
  - The Seller to use all reasonable endeavours.
  - A specific indemnity, or price protection, if Bluefen terminates or reprices for change of control.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and make it a hard, Buyer-only-waivable condition precedent.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. A consent that remains subject to conditions is not real protection.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion". The facility has change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. It is unpaid and no discharge exists.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment at Completion out of the price, as Debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - A payout letter from Riverlark.
  - Executed deeds of release, PPSR discharge (financing change statements) and release of any share security, all delivered at Completion.
  - The funds flow to show the payment going directly to Riverlark.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Make payout and release a Completion deliverable.
- **Reason:** On a debt-free basis the Buyer would otherwise pay full price for a company that still owes AUD 3.2m. The facility may also be in default on change of control.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in DD-005 Completion bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and is not in the funds flow. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses, plus all employer on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, workers' compensation and the like), treated as Debt or Transaction Costs and deducted from the price.
  - Itemisation in the funds flow, paid through Company payroll at Completion with PAYG withholding.
  - An indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Deduct the AUD 420k plus on-costs from the price.
- **Reason:** These liabilities sit in the Company the Buyer is acquiring. "A matter for the Seller" has no mechanism behind it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Clause 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. DD-004 clause 7.3 means the SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until every SOW3 fee is cleared. AUD 180,000 is open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Seller-procured payment and an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
  - A specific indemnity covering all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 IP, including third-party claims, re-development and remediation costs, and business interruption.
  - The indemnity outside the cap, basket and general time limit, and not qualified by disclosure or knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow indemnity. Require a confirmatory assignment plus a full IP indemnity.
- **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee. It is that the Company may not own core product IP.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** The SPA Update calls it "preliminary operational… not expected to be material". The letter says about 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address, and that access, scope and notifiability under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation, make any required OAIC or individual notifications, and share findings with the Buyer.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket and general time limit, for all Loss including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims.
  - A privacy/data warranty not qualified by this disclosure.
  - Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require a specific indemnity and a pre-Completion investigation.
- **Reason:** The exposure is unquantified and the seller cannot assess materiality. Regulatory penalties under the Privacy Act can be significant.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full disclosure of the terms, signing dates and approval of each renewal, and whether they were entered after the locked-box or accounts date.
  - Treatment of the renewals as a single matter.
  - If they were not ordinary course, or were entered to pre-load costs, either a price adjustment or Debt treatment for any prepaid or accrued amounts, or a specific indemnity.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant capturing renewals of this kind.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" as stated. Seek information and treat the renewals as one AUD 330k matter.
- **Reason:** The split into three equal contracts looks like it may be structured to sit below approval thresholds, or to fall below the basket individually.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims, and any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap and time limit:
  - general warranties;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, Bluefen, bonuses, Sandbar as applicable);
  - fraud.
  
  General limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. Specific indemnity claims must not be reduced by disclosure, knowledge or the basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Redraft clause 12 with express category separation.
- **Reason:** Without it, every negotiated indemnity collapses back into the AUD 4.8m cap, the AUD 250k basket and the 18-month time limit.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. The letter itself notes the Buyer has not verified this.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent verification: ASIC current and historical extract, constitution, share certificates, and confirmation of no options, convertible notes, ESOP or other rights over shares.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, with release of any Riverlark security over the shares (see SPA-N-009).
  - A fundamental title warranty as in SPA-N-004.
  - At Completion: share certificates, signed transfers, and resignations or appointments.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. Complete verification and obtain an uncapped-to-price title warranty.
- **Reason:** The register is the Seller's own record. Title failure is the single largest risk in the deal.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime", meaning a 20% cap, AUD 250k basket and 18 months.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses. It should be capped at price, run about 5–7 years or the statutory amendment period plus 6 months, have no basket, and not be qualified by disclosure.
  - IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, and employee and contractor assignments, with a longer time limit, and Ironquay handled separately (SPA-N-011).
  - Consider W&I insurance to bridge any gap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Keep tax and IP open and negotiate them as separate regimes.
- **Reason:** Tax exposures surface after 18 months as a matter of course. For a SaaS target, IP is the core asset.

---

### Other points to note
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says only notification is needed, or that the restriction is on assignment only. Have Buyer counsel confirm by reading the clauses themselves, rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.
- **Suggested next step:** Issue a full mark-up rejecting the "FINAL" framing. Lead with SPA-N-005, 004, 014, 009 and 008, because these are the structural points that determine the value of everything else.

- **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee. It is that the Company may not own core product IP.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** The SPA Update calls it "preliminary operational… not expected to be material". The letter says about 1,240 records were sent to an unintended external address, and that access, scope and notifiability under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme are all unknown.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation, make any required OAIC or individual notifications, and share findings with the Buyer.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, basket and general time limit, for all Loss including regulatory penalties to the extent lawfully indemnifiable, notification and remediation costs, and third-party and customer claims.
  - A privacy/data warranty not qualified by this disclosure.
  - Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. Require a specific indemnity and a pre-Completion investigation.
- **Reason:** The exposure is unquantified and the seller cannot assess materiality. Regulatory penalties under the Privacy Act can be significant.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". The letter does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Full disclosure of the terms, signing dates and approval of each renewal, and whether they were entered after the locked-box or accounts date.
  - Treatment of the renewals as a single matter.
  - If they were not ordinary course, or were entered to pre-load costs, either a price adjustment or Debt treatment for any prepaid or accrued amounts, or a specific indemnity.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant capturing renewals of this kind.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept "ordinary course" as stated. Seek information and treat the renewals as one AUD 330k matter.
- **Reason:** The split into three equal contracts looks like it may be structured to sit below approval thresholds, or to fall below the basket individually.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims, and any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes, each with its own cap and time limit:
  - general warranties;
  - fundamental warranties;
  - tax warranties and tax indemnity;
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, Bluefen, bonuses, Sandbar as applicable);
  - fraud.
  
  General limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. Specific indemnity claims must not be reduced by disclosure, knowledge or the basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Redraft clause 12 with express category separation.
- **Reason:** Without it, every negotiated indemnity collapses back into the AUD 4.8m cap, the AUD 250k basket and the 18-month time limit.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the DD-012 share register. The letter itself notes the Buyer has not verified this.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent verification: ASIC current and historical extract, constitution, share certificates, and confirmation of no options, convertible notes, ESOP or other rights over shares.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, with release of any Riverlark security over the shares (see SPA-N-009).
  - A fundamental title warranty as in SPA-N-004.
  - At Completion: share certificates, signed transfers, and resignations or appointments.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. Complete verification and obtain an uncapped-to-price title warranty.
- **Reason:** The register is the Seller's own record. Title failure is the single largest risk in the deal.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP "settled under the general regime", meaning a 20% cap, AUD 250k basket and 18 months.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and superannuation on the bonuses. It should be capped at price, run about 5–7 years or the statutory amendment period plus 6 months, have no basket, and not be qualified by disclosure.
  - IP warranties covering ownership, no infringement, and employee and contractor assignments, with a longer time limit, and Ironquay handled separately (SPA-N-011).
  - Consider W&I insurance to bridge any gap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled". Keep tax and IP open and negotiate them as separate regimes.
- **Reason:** Tax exposures surface after 18 months as a matter of course. For a SaaS target, IP is the core asset.

### Other points to note
- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says only notification is needed, or that the restriction is on assignment only. Have Buyer counsel confirm by reading the clauses themselves, rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.
- **Suggested next step:** Issue a full mark-up rejecting the "FINAL" framing. Lead with SPA-N-005, 004, 014, 009 and 008, because these are the structural points that determine the value of everything else.
